Silkuniene et al. (2025) from dandiset 001277¶

Paper: Silkuniene G, Silkunas M, Pakhomova ON, Semenov I, Pakhomov AG, "MHz compression of pulse packets facilitates remote focusing of electroporation", Bioelectrochemistry 166 (2025) 109016, doi:10.1016/j.bioelechem.2025.109016.

Dataset: DANDI:001277, version 0.250701.1610 (doi:10.48324/dandi.001277/0.250701.1610). The paper cites no version (its data statement says data are available on request). This is the only published version, and the draft has the same 49 assets and size and has not been modified since it was published, so the most recent published version is pinned.

Claims: claims/001277/10.1016-j.bioelechem.2025.109016.yaml, written from the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC12331426), Methods, Results and legends; no supplement.

The dandiset holds one experiment of the paper: the pulse-duration comparison of Fig. 6 (CT26 cells, packets of 300, 600 or 900 ns pulses with no interval, 2 bursts (x4)). It holds 18 wells on three plates (17 exposed and 1 sham), with a Hoechst image before exposure, a YO-PRO-1 (YP) image 30 min after it, and on two plates a propidium (Pr) and Hoechst image 2 h after it.

Claim Status here
fig6b-peak-900ns-not-significant tested
fig6c-normalized-decline-similar tested
fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak tested; blocked by its criterion when the readings differ
fig6d-600-900-differ-from-300 tested; blocked by its criterion and as it depends on the claim above
fig6d-900ns-fwhm tested; blocked as it depends on fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak
fig5-yp-lorentzian-pr-gaussian blocked, metadata insufficient (nothing links the 600-ns wells to Fig. 5); analysed as if they were the 0-mm group
fig5-yp-spot-slightly-larger-than-pr blocked and analysed, as above
fig5-raised-electrodes-weaker-centre blocked, data missing (no raised-electrode wells)
fig3-cancan-centre-enhancement, fig3-lorentzian-decline blocked, data missing (packet-rate series and controls)
fig4b-suppression-near-electrodes, fig4b-centre-no-rate-effect, fig4c-fwhm-falls-with-rate blocked, data missing (packet-rate series)
fig7be-burst-number-centre, fig7-fwhm-burst-number, fig7-sharpest-peak-1-burst-ct26 blocked, data missing (burst-number series, CHO cells)
fig2-heating-below-44c blocked, data missing (thermochromic film images)

Images are streamed from the archive and reduced as they load to 40.6-um block means (the paper's 325 x 406 um ROI is exactly 8 x 10 blocks); see cancan.py for every parameter and its source. The loading cell prints how long the streaming took and how large the files read are.

Checks of the metadata against the paper:

  • Every well is stated as "9 packets of pulses delivered at 0.2MHz", whatever its pulse duration. The dandiset's own description and the paper (Fig. 6A legend) give 18, 9 or 6 packets for 300, 600 and 900 ns, all delivered with no interval (0.4, 0.2 and 0.14 MHz). The per-file text is wrong for the 300- and 900-ns wells; the analysis uses only the pulse duration.
  • The stated inter-electrode distance, 10 mm, is the gap between the facing edges of adjacent electrodes. With 2.8-mm needles it gives a centre-to-centre side of 12.8 mm, a centre-to-centre diagonal of 18.1 mm and an edge-to-edge diagonal of 15.3 mm, the paper's figure. The two descriptions are consistent; the footprints found below check the geometry.
  • 5 wells at 300 ns, 7 at 600 ns, 5 at 900 ns and 1 sham. The paper reports n=5 per duration (Fig. 6B legend). Plate P1 row B holds the sham and two 600-ns wells; the other five plate rows each hold one well of each duration.
  • Plate P3 has no 2-h propidium image. Two files of well P2_20240925_B3 hold propidium images (checked below).

Loading the images¶

YP images of all 18 wells. Pr and the 2-h Hoechst images of the 600-ns wells that have them (the Fig. 5 claims use only these). The duplicate P2_20240925_B3 file without an object id in its name is not used. Channel 0 of the Cy3-DAPI files is Pr and channel 1 Hoechst: the OME metadata of each file name them Cy3 (emission 565 nm) and DAPI (455 nm), printed below the loading cell.

In [5]:
fitc = files[files.series == "Imaging_FITC"].set_index("well")
cy = files[(files.series == "Imaging_Cy3-DAPI") & files.path.str.contains("_obj-")].set_index("well")
pr_wells = [w for w in cy.index if cy.loc[w, "pulse_ns"] == 600]
jobs = [(fitc.loc[w, "asset_id"], None) for w in wells.well]
jobs += [(cy.loc[w, "asset_id"], 0) for w in pr_wells] + [(cy.loc[w, "asset_id"], 1) for w in pr_wells]
import time
t0 = time.time()
loaded = cc.load_many(jobs, workers=4)
print("loading took %.1f min" % ((time.time() - t0) / 60))
yp = {w: loaded[i][0] for i, w in enumerate(wells.well)}
k = len(wells)
pr = {w: loaded[k + i][0] for i, w in enumerate(pr_wells)}
hoechst2h = {w: loaded[k + len(pr_wells) + i][0] for i, w in enumerate(pr_wells)}
sat = {w: loaded[i][1] for i, w in enumerate(wells.well)}
top = {w: loaded[i][2] for i, w in enumerate(wells.well)}
print("YP images:", len(yp), " Pr images:", len(pr), pr_wells)
print("block image shape:", yp[wells.well[0]].shape, "block size %.4f mm" % cc.BLOCK_MM)
print("size of the files loaded: %.1f GB (%d YP files, %d Cy3-DAPI files)"
      % (fitc.loc[wells.well, "size_gb"].sum() + cy.loc[pr_wells, "size_gb"].sum(), len(wells), len(pr_wells)))

# channel order of the Cy3-DAPI files, from the OME metadata of each file used
import re
for w in pr_wells:
    h = cc.open_nwb(cy.loc[w, "asset_id"])
    ome = h["acquisition/Imaging_Cy3-DAPI"].attrs["description"]
    ch = re.findall(r'Channel ID="Channel:(\d)" Name="([^"]+)".*?EmissionWavelength="([^"]+)"', ome)
    print(w, ["channel %s %s (emission %s nm)" % c for c in ch])
print("Cy3-DAPI files (one per well) by pulse duration:", cy.pulse_ns.fillna(0).astype(int).value_counts().sort_index().to_dict(),
      "(0 = sham)")

})

The OME metadata of every file gives 12 significant bits, but pixel values in the YP images run far above 4095 (the largest block means are 3500 to 22600), so the stored values are not raw 12-bit camera counts (perhaps rescaled by the stitching software). The analysis uses background-subtracted differences and ratios within each image, which a common scale factor does not change. Unimaged corners of the stitched mosaic are zeros and are not used.

Electrode footprints and the array centre¶

The paper measures from the geometrical centre of the array along the diagonals joining the footprints (Methods 2.5). The footprints are found in each image (cc.find_electrodes). The footprint centre-to-centre diagonal implied by Methods 2.2 is 18.1 mm (15.3 mm between facing edges plus one 2.8-mm diameter), and the diagonals should be perpendicular. As a check that the centre found from the footprints is where the YP response is, the brightest point of the smoothed YP image within 5 mm of the centre is compared with it, and with 1000 random points at the same radius from the image centre. The YP image is clipped at its 99.5th percentile and smoothed (sigma 0.5 mm) first, so that bright debris does not count as the peak.

In [8]:
from scipy import ndimage

meas = {}
geo_rows = []
for w in wells.well:
    sham = bool(wells.set_index("well").loc[w, "sham"])
    m = cc.measure_well(yp[w])
    meas[w] = m
    g = m["geom"]
    sm = ndimage.gaussian_filter(np.minimum(yp[w], np.percentile(yp[w], 99.5)), 12)
    c = g["centre"]
    r = int(5 / cc.BLOCK_MM)
    sub = sm[int(c[0]) - r:int(c[0]) + r, int(c[1]) - r:int(c[1]) + r]
    pk = np.array(np.unravel_index(np.argmax(sub), sub.shape)) + [int(c[0]) - r, int(c[1]) - r]
    geo_rows.append({"well": w, "pulse_ns": wells.set_index("well").loc[w, "pulse_ns"], "sham": sham,
                     "diag1_mm": g["diag_lengths_mm"][0], "diag2_mm": g["diag_lengths_mm"][1],
                     "angle_deg": g["diag_angle_deg"], "min_rim_contrast": min(g["contrast"]),
                     "peak_offset_mm": float(np.hypot(*(pk - c)) * cc.BLOCK_MM),
                     "background": m[("bg", "darkest")], "background_all4": m[("bg", "all")]})

# reference: distance from the YP peak to random points 0 to 3 mm from the image centre
rng = np.random.default_rng(1277)
ref = []
for w in geo[ok].index:
    sm = ndimage.gaussian_filter(np.minimum(yp[w], np.percentile(yp[w], 99.5)), 12)
    c = meas[w]["geom"]["centre"]
    r = int(5 / cc.BLOCK_MM)
    sub = sm[int(c[0]) - r:int(c[0]) + r, int(c[1]) - r:int(c[1]) + r]
    pk = np.array(np.unravel_index(np.argmax(sub), sub.shape)) + [int(c[0]) - r, int(c[1]) - r]
    n = yp[w].shape[0]
    ang = rng.uniform(0, 2 * np.pi, 1000)
    rad = rng.uniform(0, 3 / cc.BLOCK_MM, 1000)
    pts = np.c_[(n - 1) / 2 + rad * np.sin(ang), (n - 1) / 2 + rad * np.cos(ang)]
    ref.append(np.median(np.hypot(*(pts - pk).T)) * cc.BLOCK_MM)
print("median distance from the YP peak to random points within 3 mm of the image centre: %.2f mm (range %.2f to %.2f)"
      % (np.median(ref), np.min(ref), np.max(ref)))

The footprints are found in all 17 exposed wells, with diagonals of 17.7 to 18.5 mm against the 18.1 mm the paper's geometry implies, and close to perpendicular; the sham well has no footprints (no electrodes visible) and is not used. In 16 of the 17 exposed wells the YP peak lies within 0.42 mm of the centre found from the footprints, against a median of 1.7 mm to random points near the image centre; the exception is P1_20240926_B2, whose uptake covers the whole array. This is consistent with the paper's geometry and the alignment of ROIs to the array, which is the spatial counterpart of a clock check for these single-time-point images (there are no trial tables or time series). Distances along a diagonal are scaled so that the footprint centre is at 9.05 mm; the measured footprint diagonals, above, show the scale of the stitched images agrees with the stated 1.625 um per pixel within 3%.

Two 600-ns wells on plate P1, row B (P1_20240926_B2 and B3), show YP uptake over the whole array, unlike the other 15 exposed wells. Their profiles are shown next.

Which wells form Fig. 6 (assumption)¶

The paper reports n=5 per pulse duration; the dandiset has 7 wells at 600 ns. Neither the paper nor the dandiset says which five were used. The plate layout gives a basis that does not depend on the results: five plate rows (P1 row A, P2 rows A and B, P3 rows A and B) each hold one well of 300, 600 and 900 ns, which is one complete experiment per row and gives exactly n=5 per duration. The sixth row, P1 row B, holds the sham well and two more 600-ns wells. The main reading takes the five complete rows; it is an assumption, and each Fig. 6 claim also shows the result with all 7 wells at 600 ns and with every choice of 5 of the 7. The two P1 row B wells also differ in their images (uptake over the whole array, above) and P1_20240926_B3 shows a loss of Hoechst-stained cells over the centre at 2 h (below), the paper's check for detachment (Methods 2.4).

def fw(wset, spacing, half, pooling, bg="darkest"):
    return {d: np.array([cc.fwhm(meas[w], spacing, half, pooling, bg)["fwhm"] for w in wset[d]]) for d in (300, 600, 900)}

def sets_for(sub):
    return {300: main[300], 600: sub, 900: main[900]}

readings = list(itertools.product(cc.SPACINGS, cc.HALF_RANGES, cc.POOLINGS))
fits_failed = sum(not cc.fwhm(meas[w], s, h, p)["ok"] for w in geo[ok].index for s, h, p in readings)

fig6b-peak-900ns-not-significant¶

The central peak of YP uptake is highest for 900-ns pulse packets, but its difference from 300- and 600-ns packets is not statistically significant.

Per well, background-subtracted YP at the centre ROI. Readings of the criterion: (a) two-sided t-tests of 900 against 300 and against 600 ns, Bonferroni over the three pairwise comparisons; (b) one-way ANOVA over the three durations. The centre value from the Lorentzian fit (parameter a, 1-mm steps, -5 to 5 mm) is a variant. The ROI spacing does not change the centre ROI.

In [14]:
def fig6b(wset, bg="darkest", use_fit=False):
    if use_fit:
        c = {d: np.array([cc.fwhm(meas[w], "1mm", 5.0, "avg", bg)["a"] for w in wset[d]]) for d in (300, 600, 900)}
    else:
        c = {d: np.array([cc.centre_value(meas[w], "1mm", bg) for w in wset[d]]) for d in (300, 600, 900)}
    ms = {d: cc.mean_se(c[d]) for d in c}
    t9_3 = cc.ttest_bonf(c[900], c[300], 3)
    t9_6 = cc.ttest_bonf(c[900], c[600], 3)
    t6_3 = cc.ttest_bonf(c[600], c[300], 3)
    an = stats.f_oneway(c[300], c[600], c[900])
    top = max(ms, key=lambda d: ms[d][0])
    return {"mean_se": {d: (round(ms[d][0], 1), round(ms[d][1], 1), len(c[d])) for d in ms}, "highest": top,
            "p_bonf 900v300": t9_3["p_bonf"], "p_bonf 900v600": t9_6["p_bonf"], "p_bonf 600v300": t6_3["p_bonf"],
            "d 900v300": t9_3["cohen_d"], "d 900v600": t9_6["cohen_d"], "anova F": float(an.statistic), "anova p": float(an.pvalue)}

for name, ws, kw in [("main (5 complete rows)", main, {}), ("all 7 at 600 ns", all7, {}),
                     ("main, background from all 4 footprints", main, {"bg": "all"}),
                     ("main, centre from Lorentzian a", main, {"use_fit": True})]:
    r = fig6b(ws, **kw)
    print(name)
    print("  centre YP mean, s.e., n:", r["mean_se"], " highest:", r["highest"])

    print("  (b) ANOVA F = %.2f, p = %.3f" % (r["anova F"], r["anova p"]))

Result: reproduced, with the five complete plate rows as the Fig. 6 wells (assumption). Centre YP is highest at 900 ns (899 against 551 at 300 ns and 866 at 600 ns, camera units), and no test finds a difference: the Bonferroni-corrected p of 900 against 300 ns is 0.975 and against 600 ns 1.000 (Cohen's d 0.66 and 0.05), and the ANOVA p is 0.54. The same holds with all 7 wells at 600 ns, with the background from all four footprints, and with the fitted centre value. Over the 21 choices of 5 of the 7 600-ns wells no test is significant, but 900 ns is highest in only 14. Centre YP differs more between plates than between durations (P3 is 2.1 to 4.6 times P1 and P2 at the same duration). The criterion's unpaired tests ignore that each plate row is one experiment; treating the rows as blocks, paired t-tests give Bonferroni p of 0.415 (900 against 300 ns) and 1.000 (900 against 600 ns), and a repeated-measures ANOVA gives p = 0.071, so this variant also finds no difference.

fig6c-normalized-decline-similar¶

With the peak YP emission taken as 100%, the decline of YP emission away from the centre looks similar for 300-, 600- and 900-ns pulses.

Per well, the profile (two diagonals averaged) in percent of its value at 0 mm; mean and s.e. per duration at each distance. Two durations differ at a distance when the gap between their s.e. bars is longer than the bars (Methods 2.5; the mean of the two bar lengths, Cumming et al. 2007, is used when they differ, and the longer bar is shown as a variant). Readings: distances -5 to 5 mm or every measured distance (to 7 mm), and 1-mm steps or contiguous ROIs.

def fig6c(wset, spacing, lim, bar="mean"):
    x, _ = meas[wset[300][0]][("darkest", spacing)]
    i0 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(x)))
    norm = {d: np.array([100 * meas[w][("darkest", spacing)][1].mean(0) / meas[w][("darkest", spacing)][1].mean(0)[i0]
                         for w in wset[d]]) for d in (300, 600, 900)}
    hits = []
    sel = np.where((np.abs(x) <= lim + 1e-9) & (np.arange(len(x)) != i0))[0]
    for a, b in itertools.combinations((300, 600, 900), 2):
        for i in sel:
            ma, sa = cc.mean_se(norm[a][:, i])
            mb, sb = cc.mean_se(norm[b][:, i])
            gap = max(mb - sb - (ma + sa), ma - sa - (mb + sb))
            thr = (sa + sb) / 2 if bar == "mean" else max(sa, sb)
            if gap > thr:
                hits.append((a, b, round(float(x[i]), 2), round(ma, 1), round(mb, 1), round(gap, 1), round(thr, 1)))
    return norm, x, hits

                      % (name, spacing, lim, bar, len(hits)), hits)

Result: not reproduced. Under every reading (both ROI spacings, both distance ranges, both bar rules, the main wells or all 7 at 600 ns, and every choice of 5 of the 7) at least one distance shows two durations separated by a gap longer than the s.e. bars. Over the 16 readings with the main wells or all 7, 52 of the 96 gaps are between 300 and 900 ns, 36 between 300 and 600 ns and 8 between 600 and 900 ns. Every reading has a 300 against 900 ns gap at 1 to 2 mm from the centre, where the 900-ns profile falls faster (19.6% against 12.5% of the centre at +2 mm with 1-mm steps, gap 4.6 against bars of 1.3), and every choice of 5 of the 7 wells has the same 300 against 900 ns gaps under every reading (they do not involve the 600-ns wells). With the main wells and contiguous ROIs most gaps (8 of 12 to 14) are between 300 and 600 ns, at 1.6 to 4.9 mm; with distances to 7 mm, 900 ns also lies above 300 ns at 6.9 or 7 mm. The narrowing near the centre is the sharper peak at longer pulses that the paper reports in Fig. 6D; by the error-bar rule the criterion names, the declines are not similar.

fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak¶

FWHM of the central YP peak, fitted per experiment, decreases with pulse duration from 300 to 900 ns, with a trend slope different from zero (p = 0.003).

Per well, the Lorentzian of Methods 2.5 fitted by least squares (centre at 0, no offset); FWHM is b. FWHM is regressed on pulse duration (linear, Fig. 6D legend, or on log duration, Results 3.3), over the 15 individual values or the 3 means, with the two-sided t-test of the slope. Further readings: fit half-range 4, 5 or 6 mm; 1-mm or contiguous ROIs; the diagonals averaged before fitting, or all points fitted (these two give the same least-squares fit when both diagonals are sampled at the same distances, as here).

def fig6d_slopes(wset):
    rows = []
    for spacing, half, pooling in readings:
        f = fw(wset, spacing, half, pooling)
        xs = np.concatenate([[d] * len(f[d]) for d in (300, 600, 900)])
        ys = np.concatenate([f[d] for d in (300, 600, 900)])
        means = np.array([f[d].mean() for d in (300, 600, 900)])
        for points in ("individual", "means"):
            for trend in ("linear", "log"):
                xx = (np.array([300, 600, 900]) if points == "means" else xs).astype(float)
                yy = means if points == "means" else ys
                st = cc.slope_test(np.log(xx) if trend == "log" else xx, yy)
                rows.append({"spacing": spacing, "half_mm": half, "pooling": pooling, "points": points, "trend": trend,
                             "fwhm300": f[300].mean(), "fwhm600": f[600].mean(), "fwhm900": f[900].mean(),
                             "slope": st["slope"], "p": st["p"], "r": st["r"], "n": st["n"]})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

t_main = fig6d_slopes(main)

print("negative slope with p < 0.05 in %d of %d readings; p range %.4f to %.4f"
      % (neg.sum(), len(t_main), t_main.p.min(), t_main.p.max()))

Result: blocked (methods underspecified): the readings differ, which the criterion says blocks the claim. With the five complete plate rows, mean FWHM falls from 2.10 to 2.14 mm at 300 ns to 1.80 to 1.91 mm at 600 ns and 1.69 to 1.80 mm at 900 ns, and the slope is negative under all 48 readings. It is significant (p < 0.05) under 28: every reading fitted to the 15 individual values with contiguous ROIs (p 0.0020 to 0.0037, close to the paper's 0.003), 10 of 12 with 1-mm steps (p 0.042 to 0.048; the other two give 0.050), and the log trend on the 3 means with 1-mm steps (p 0.012 to 0.016); the other readings on 3 means give p 0.08 to 0.18. FWHM falls with duration on each plate. With all 7 wells at 600 ns the slope is significant under none of the 48 readings (p 0.83 to 1.00), as the two P1 row B wells have FWHMs of about 5 and 18 mm; of the 21 choices of 5 of the 7, only the one that leaves out both of them gives a significant slope. The outcome therefore depends on leaving out the two P1 row B wells: with either of them kept, the slope is significant under no reading and the claim would be not reproduced, so the block rests on the assumption about the wells. With distances from the OME pixel size instead of scaling the footprint centre to 9.05 mm (cell under fig6d-900ns-fwhm), the linear slope on the 15 values gives p 0.0044 to 0.0051 with contiguous ROIs and 0.040 to 0.045 with 1-mm steps, the same pattern. Contiguous ROIs overlap (a 0.406-mm step along a diagonal near 45 degrees moves an axis-aligned box 0.29 mm along each axis), which does not enter the slope test on per-well FWHMs.

fig6d-600-900-differ-from-300¶

FWHM for 600-ns and for 900-ns packets is each significantly smaller than for 300-ns packets (Bonferroni-corrected t-tests, p = 0.028 for one and p = 0.0072 for the other).

Two-sided Student's t-tests of 600 against 300 ns and 900 against 300 ns, Bonferroni over 2 or 3 comparisons, under every reading of ROI spacing, fit range and pooling.

In [22]:
def fig6d_pairs(wset):
    rows = []
    for spacing, half, pooling in readings:
        f = fw(wset, spacing, half, pooling)
        for m in (2, 3):
            a = cc.ttest_bonf(f[600], f[300], m)
            b = cc.ttest_bonf(f[900], f[300], m)
            rows.append({"spacing": spacing, "half_mm": half, "pooling": pooling, "m": m,
                         "p600v300": a["p_bonf"], "diff600": a["diff"], "d600": a["cohen_d"],
                         "p900v300": b["p_bonf"], "diff900": b["diff"], "d900": b["cohen_d"]})
    t = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    t["n_significant"] = ((t.p600v300 < 0.05) & (t.diff600 < 0)).astype(int) + ((t.p900v300 < 0.05) & (t.diff900 < 0)).astype(int)
    return t

p_main = fig6d_pairs(main)

All 7 at 600 ns: readings with both significant 0, one 12, none 12; 600v300 corrected p 0.686 to 1.000

Result: blocked (methods underspecified), as the criterion requires when readings differ, and because it depends on fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak, which is blocked. In the main wells, 900 against 300 ns is significant after correction with contiguous ROIs (p 0.0053 to 0.0089, close to the paper's 0.0072) but not with 1-mm steps (p 0.077 to 0.131), and 600 against 300 ns is significant under no reading (p 0.058 to 0.092 with contiguous ROIs, 0.44 to 0.66 with 1-mm steps, against the paper's 0.028). The readings give one significant comparison or none; FWHM is smaller at both longer durations under every reading (Cohen's d -0.84 to -2.71). With unscaled distances the Bonferroni p over 2 comparisons is 0.0087 to 0.0096 (900 against 300 ns) and 0.091 to 0.092 (600 against 300 ns) with contiguous ROIs, and 0.067 to 0.076 and 0.31 to 0.32 with 1-mm steps.

    st = cc.slope_test(xs, np.concatenate([f[d] for d in (300, 600, 900)]))
    rows.append({"spacing": spacing, "half_mm": half, "pooling": pooling, "fwhm900_mean": m, "fwhm900_se": s,
                 "pct_of_15.3": 100 * m / cc.DIAGONAL_GAP_MM,
                 "both_ok": abs(m - 1.7) <= 0.08 + 1e-12 and abs(100 * m / 15.3 - 11.1) <= 0.6 + 1e-12,
                 "slope p (15 values, linear)": st["p"], "slope": st["slope"],
                 "p_bonf 600v300 (2)": cc.ttest_bonf(f[600], f[300], 2)["p_bonf"],
                 "p_bonf 900v300 (2)": cc.ttest_bonf(f[900], f[300], 2)["p_bonf"]})
tu = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Unscaled distances, main wells:")
print(tu.round(4).to_string())
print("900-ns readings with both values within tolerance: %d of %d" % (tu.both_ok.sum(), len(tu)))

Result: blocked (methods underspecified), because it depends on fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak, which is blocked (docs/protocol.md, Author, step 1.5: a claim that depends on a blocked claim is blocked for the same reason). Its own criterion would be met: with contiguous ROIs the mean 900-ns FWHM is 1.69 to 1.71 mm (s.e. 0.08 to 0.09), 11.0 to 11.1% of 15.3 mm, within both tolerances under all six contiguous readings. With 1-mm steps it is 1.78 to 1.80 mm, just above the upper bound of 1.78 mm. With distances from the OME pixel size, unscaled, it is 1.69 to 1.71 mm with contiguous ROIs (within both tolerances in 6 of 12 readings) and 1.81 to 1.83 mm with 1-mm steps. The block comes from the parent claim, whose block rests on the assumption about the 600-ns wells, so this block rests on it too.

Fig. 5 at 0-mm elevation: the 600-ns wells¶

Fig. 5 compares YP and Pr with the electrodes touching the monolayer (0 mm) or raised. Its 0-mm condition is the MHz-CANCAN protocol, 600-ns packets with no interval, 2 bursts (x4), CT26 cells (Results 3.2), the same protocol as the dandiset's 600-ns wells, which also have Pr images on plates P1 and P2. The Fig. 5 legend gives n=6-7 for YP and n=4-5 for Pr; the dandiset has 7 YP and 5 Pr wells at 600 ns. Nothing in the dandiset links these wells to Fig. 5: its title and description name only the pulse-duration experiment, the raised-electrode wells of the same series are absent, and Pr images exist also for three 300-ns and three 900-ns wells. The two Fig. 5 claims are therefore blocked (metadata insufficient). The analysis below shows what they would give if the 600-ns wells were Fig. 5's 0-mm group. Readings: YP from all 7 wells or the 5 main ones; Pr from all 5 wells, the 4 without P1_20240926_B3, or the 3 in the main rows; 1-mm or contiguous ROIs. Fits are to the mean profile over wells (two diagonals averaged per well), from -5 to 5 mm (Results 3.2); R2 does not depend on the scaling to 100%.

def fit_offset(x, y, kind, half=5.0):
    m = np.abs(x) <= half + 1e-9
    xs, ys = x[m], y[m]
    f = (lambda x, a, b, c: cc.lorentz(x, a, b) + c) if kind == "lorentz" else (lambda x, a, s, c: cc.gauss(x, a, s) + c)
    p, _ = optimize.curve_fit(f, xs, ys, p0=(ys.max() - ys.min(), 2.0, ys.min()), maxfev=20000)
    pred = f(xs, *p)
    fw = abs(p[1]) * (1 if kind == "lorentz" else 2.4)
    return 1 - ((ys - pred) ** 2).sum() / ((ys - ys.mean()) ** 2).sum(), fw, p[2]

rows = []
for spacing in cc.SPACINGS:
    for pname, pset in (("Pr 5 wells", pr_wells), ("Pr 3 main", [w for w in pr_wells if w in main[600]])):
        xp, mp = mean_profile(pr_meas, pset, spacing)
        for kind in ("lorentz", "gauss"):
            r2, fwo, c0 = fit_offset(xp, mp, kind)
            rows.append({"spacing": spacing, "Pr set": pname, "kind": kind, "R2 with offset": r2,
                         "R2 no offset": cc.fit_curve(xp, mp, kind, 5.0)["r2"], "FWHM with offset": fwo,
                         "offset as % of centre": 100 * c0 / mp[np.argmin(abs(xp))]})
print()
print("Fits to the mean Pr profile, -5 to 5 mm, with and without a constant offset:")

The Pr images are not clean central spots. Per well, Pr within 5 mm of the centre averages 40 to 53% of the centre value in the three main-row wells and about 100% in the two P1 row B wells, so the mean profile sits on a broad pedestal. With a constant offset added, the Gaussian fits the mean Pr profile better than the Lorentzian under all 4 readings shown (2 ROI spacings by 2 Pr well sets, 8 fits; R2 0.935 to 0.979 against 0.922 to 0.972), with offsets of 30 to 48% of the centre and Gaussian FWHMs of 3.2 to 3.6 mm; without it, the Lorentzian fits better. The Methods' fits have no offset, so whether these Pr data are comparable with the paper's cannot be settled from the dandiset. In the Pr images the weakest footprint has a rim contrast of 74 to 76 in P1_20240926_B3 and P2_20240925_A3 against 193 to 416 in the other three, so the footprints are located less reliably there (two marks in P1_20240926_B3 fall on no visible footprint in the figure above).

Result: blocked (metadata insufficient): nothing links the dandiset's 600-ns wells to Fig. 5. If they were its 0-mm group, the claim would fail as the criterion states it: the Lorentzian fits YP better than the Gaussian under all 12 readings (R2 0.93 to 0.99 against 0.75 to 0.97), but it also fits Pr better under all 12 (R2 0.81 to 0.95 against 0.72 to 0.86), the reverse of the paper, and the Pr Gaussian R2 is within its tolerance (0.864 to 1.056) under none. With an offset the ordering for Pr reverses (cell above). The "max fit p" treats overlapping contiguous ROIs as independent and understates p for those readings.

Parts of blocked claims the dandiset can inform¶

The claims below are blocked because the dandiset lacks the packet-rate, raised-electrode, burst-number and thermometry experiments. Two quantities they mention can be measured on the 600-ns wells, which use the 0.2-MHz, 2-burst (x4) protocol: the ratio of centre to near-electrode YP (fig4b-suppression-near-electrodes, 40-fold) and near-electrode YP as percent of the centre at 0 mm (fig5-raised-electrodes-weaker-centre). They are shown, not judged: the wells are not the experiments of Fig. 4.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's: ROIs are placed by an algorithm on the footprints it finds, not by eye in MetaMorph, and are rounded to a 40.6-um grid; distances are scaled so the footprint centre is 9.05 mm from the centre (unscaled distances, run for the three fig6d claims, give the same outcomes for them); the ROI spacing, fit range and the wells of the 600-ns group are not given by the paper and are run under every reading; the background ROIs are in the darkest footprint.

What was found about the dandiset: it holds only the pulse-duration experiment (Fig. 6, and perhaps the 0-mm wells of Fig. 5, which nothing in it identifies); every well's description gives 9 packets at 0.2 MHz whatever the pulse duration; it has 7 wells at 600 ns where the paper analysed 5, with nothing to say which; two of them (P1 row B) show uptake across the whole array, and with them the Fig. 6D trend is absent; one propidium image is deposited twice (P2_20240925_B3); plate P3 has no propidium images; pixel size and the electrode geometry agree with the paper.
